1. This will enable the client to close gap to market parity by oﬀering net new claim document upload (close market gap with speed; iteratively)

2. Drive some operational eﬃciencies in the AS and Datacap teams

## Provide a secure method to provide net new claim form


4. Simplify claim submission process for plan sponsors and enhance visibility of claim submission. Problem Statement Plan sponsors currently lack a streamlined, digital method to submit new claim documents, resulting in limited visibility, and potential delays in during the submission process. The absence of an end-to-end submission process creates a gap in the client's service oﬀering compared to market competitors. Additionally, the current process places operational strain on internal teams such as AS and Datacap, and lacks a secure, user-friendly mechanism for submitting and conﬁrming receipt of claim documentation. This hinders both the sponsor experience and internal eﬃciency. In-Scope

1. Upload of PDF document and other document formats (jpg, jpeg, png)

2. Anything not explicitly stated in-scope. High-Level Requirements (Features)

1. The system will allow submission of a document (at a minimum) in PDF format including jpg, jpeg, png.

2. The system will allow users to upload an Employer Form document and attach all metadata associated with the form.

3. The system will allow users to upload multiple documents simultaneously and attach all meta-data to each uploaded document.

4. The system will convert uploaded document into the required format to meet internal system speciﬁcations and ensure compatibility with downstream processing.

5. The system will ingest and store the document in applicable repository.

6. The system will route the document as needed to relevant workﬂows within existing sources without human intervention.

7. The system will pre-populate some basic information for the user, based on pre-deﬁned parameters.

8. The system will provide data validation for basic formatting and completeness based on pre-deﬁned formatting requirements

9. The system will provide users with a conﬁrmation of successful or failed uploads and include the expected timeline claim will be visible on the dashboard.

10. The system will delete all ﬁles that have not been submitted by the user to prevent any downstream processing, storage, or retention of those ﬁles.

11. The system will invoke exception-handling when errors occur after a successful submission conﬁrmation has been provided to the user, ensuring the ﬁle proceeds through the workﬂow and is stored without downstream failures.

12. The system will perform scheduled clean-up of abandoned or stale ﬁles in accordance with organizational data retention policies or retention rules deﬁned by project stakeholders. Acceptance Criteria (Each criterion is numbered “1.” in the source; headings below keep the source order.) Document Submission Format

- Given the user is on the document upload interface

- When they upload a document

- Then the system will accept the document at a minimum in PDF format including jpg, jpeg, png. (TBD)

- And reject unsupported formats with a clear error message Upload Employer Form document with metadata

- Given the user is on the document upload interface

- When the user wants to submit an Employer Form and provides relevant metadata

- Then the system should upload the document

- And associate the metadata with the Employer Form uploaded Upload additional multiple document with metadata

- Given the user is on the document upload interface

- When the user selects multiple document and provides relevant metadata for each document

- Then the system should upload all selected document simultaneously

- And associate the correct metadata with each uploaded document Document Conversion

- Given a user uploads a document to the sponsor portal

- When the system receives the document

- Then the system shall automatically convert the document into the format required by internal systems

- And ensure the converted document meets compatibility standards for downstream processing Document Ingestion and Storage

- Given a valid document is submitted

- When the upload is successful

- Then the system will ingest and store the document (securely e.g. AV scan) in the applicable repository Routing

- Given a document has been successfully stored

- When routing rules are triggered

- Then the system will automatically route the document to the appropriate workﬂow(s)

- And do so without requiring manual intervention Pre-populate Basic Information

- Given the user is authenticated and initiating a document upload

- When the document upload process is in progress

- Then system shall pre-populate basic information

- And based on pre-deﬁned parameters Data Validation

- Given the user engages the claim submission process

- When they attempt to submit

- Then the system shall validate the data for: Required ﬁelds Correct formatting (e.g., date, numeric, text ﬁelds as per requirements) Document attached

- And display clear error messages for any validation failures Upload Conﬁrmation and Timeline

- Given a document is uploaded

- When the upload is processed

- Then the system shall: Display a conﬁrmation message indicating success or failure Provide a reference number for tracking Include an estimated timeline for when the claim will be visible on the dashboard User-removed ﬁles

- Given a user has uploaded one or more ﬁles but has not yet submitted them

- And the ﬁles are still in the pre-submission state

- When the user chooses to delete a ﬁle

- Then the system shall remove the selected ﬁle from the session

- And the deleted ﬁle shall not be stored, processed, or retained in any system repository. Exception Handling

- Given a ﬁle has been submitted for processing by the user

- And a successful submission conﬁrmation has been provided to the user

- And the system encounters an error during the processing of that ﬁle

- Then the system shall invoke exception handling process

- And the ﬁle shall proceed through the processing workﬂow and be stored in the repository without downstream failures Cleanup: Abandoned and or Stale Files

- Given a user has uploaded a document and never submitted it

- Or a user session has timed out and the ﬁles are abandoned

- When organizational data retention rules indicate such ﬁles are eligible for removal

- Then the system shall delete those unsubmitted, abandoned, or stale ﬁles

- And no trace of those ﬁles shall remain stored beyond the retention threshold

- And this cleanup process shall occur without requiring user action. Dependencies Authentication services Document Management systems Claim Management System File size – will follow MCLAW standard and not going above or beyond. FAQ
